LESSON: SIGN READING 13.2.1 EXTENSIVE SIGN READING: NEWSPAPERS/MAGAZINES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.2: Sign Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Newspapers/Magazines
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Newspapers/Magazines, part of Strand 13 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to read newspapers and magazines? 2. How do we choose the materials we read? 3. When do we read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Newspapers/Magazines together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: learner develops the skill of teamwork as they set up after-school clubs for reading purposes.

• Learning to learn: learner develops the skill of independent learning as they look for information on their own.

Values:
Responsibility: hard work, as learners sign read the children’s section of a newspaper or magazine and later writes their own stories or articles.

Link to other subjects

Learners relate the concept of extensive sign reading to their learning in Kiswahili, creative arts, social studies and RE
